stem: Where did Lord Sinha resign from the post of Governor in 1921?
expl: Satyendra Prasanna Sinha was born on 24 March, 1863, at Raipur in Birbhum, Bengal. He was the first Indian to be appointed Advocate General of Bengal in 1905. His appointment to this post was confirmed in 1908. In 1920, he was appointed Governor of Bihar and Orissa, and he was the first Indian to obtain this post in administration. Due to health reasons, he resigned from his post in 1921. He died on 4 March, 1928.

stem: Which of the following Acts converted the Unicameral Legislature of Bihar into Bicameral : Bihar Legislative Assembly and Bihar Legislative Council?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: On the basis of the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935, Bihar and Odisha were separated and made two provinces, and provincial autonomy was introduced. Under the provisions of this Act, bicameral legislatures were established in six provinces (Madras, Bombay, Bengal, United Provinces, Bihar and Assam). Accordingly, Bihar’s unicameral legislature was converted into a bicameral legislature—the Bihar Legislative Assembly and the Bihar Legislative Council. Under this arrangement, the then existing Provincial Legislative Council was renamed as the Bihar Legislative Assembly, and the Bihar Legislative Council was constituted as the upper house.

expl: On the basis of the Government of India Act, 1935, provincial legislature elections were held in February, 1937. In July 1937, the Congress formed ministries in six provinces—Madras, Bombay, Central Provinces and Berar, Odisha, Bihar and the United Provinces. Later, Congress also formed ministries with allied parties in the North-West Frontier Province and Assam. stem: When did Baldev Sahay resign from the post of Advocate General?
expl: The failures of the August Offer (August 1940) and the Cripps Mission (1942) ultimately gave rise to the Quit India Movement. During this period, when the demand for the formation of a national government was rejected, the Wardha Resolution was reaffirmed at the meeting of the All India Congress Committee held at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, on 7–8 August, 1942. As soon as the Quit India Movement began on 9 August, 1942, the British government arrested all top-level Congress leaders under Operation Zero Hour. In protest against this, Bihar’s Advocate General, Baldev Sahay, resigned from his post in 1942.
